slot.brief: Solve a variable separable DE of the form dy/dx = f(x)g(y) and apply an initial condition to find the constant.

stem: The solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x+1}{y+2}$ satisfying $y(0)=0$ has $y(1)$ equal to

verdicts.working: Separate and integrate: $(y+2)^2=(x+1)^2+C$. Using $y(0)=0$ gives $C=3$. The solution follows the positive branch since $y(0)+2=2>0$, so $y(1)=\sqrt7-2$.

working:
$$(y+2)\,dy=(x+1)\,dx$$
$$\frac{y^2}{2}+2y=\frac{x^2}{2}+x+C$$
$y(0)=0\Rightarrow C=0$.
At $x=1$: $y^2+4y-3=0$, so $y=-2\pm\sqrt{7}$.
The solution through $y(0)=0$ is the positive branch; hence $y(1)=\sqrt{7}-2$.
